idea: How to maintain a water tank
title: Prevent Sediment Build-Up with Regular Tank Scouring
description: An educational breakdown explaining why water storage tanks require periodic flushing via the bottom drain valve to protect household plumbing and maintain water quality.
image_prompt: A professional educational photo of a vertical polyethylene water storage tank mounted on a sturdy concrete platform outdoors under bright daytime light. The side of the tank features a clean cutaway visual view illustrating the lower interior section. At the very floor of the tank lies a layer of settled dark fine sediment and silt. Positioned flush with the tank floor is a bottom drain line with a brass ball valve releasing cloudy, silty water into a floor drain below. A few inches higher on the tank wall, a separate clean domestic water supply pipe with a red handle shut-off valve is positioned clearly above the sediment level. Realistic PPR and PVC piping connections with proper union fittings and wall clamps. Clean vertical 9:16 composition with ample uncluttered background space in the top and bottom thirds for text placement. Photorealistic style, crisp lighting, physically accurate plumbing layout. No text, no logos, no watermarks, no brand names, no fake labels, no diagrams.
visual_story: The visual highlights the critical height difference between the tank's bottom drain (scour line) and the domestic supply outlet line. Viewers can see how fine sand and rust particles settle at the floor of the tank below the supply line. By opening the lowest valve, sediment is purged without allowing contaminated heavy sludge into the elevated supply pipe that feeds household fixtures.

on_image_text.hook: Sediment at the bottom of your tank affects your entire water supply.
on_image_text.explanation: Heavy particles settle at the tank floor, building up until they reach the supply outlet pipe.
on_image_text.takeaway: Flush the bottom scour valve every six months until water runs clear.
